newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday April 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday April 29.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Italy's governing centre-left coalition suffer a setback as results show opposition candidates leading in the first round of mayoral elections in two big northern cities, but made stronger showings in other areas. Most of the elections in more than 100 cities and towns with a population of more than 15,000 will have to go to a run-off on May 11 (all).

* Hard-left Communist Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti said the good showing by his party in Sunday's local elections would strengthen the party's hand in coming negotiations on welfare reforms (all).

* Foreign minister Lamberto Dini said Italy must cut government spending, even if it meant doing so with a different government majority. Dini added his support and that of his party for the government led by Romano Prodi was conditioned on its succeeding in achieving promised budget consolidation (all).

* Centre-right opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi indicated that his Freedom Alliance would not make any deals to help prime minister Romano Prodi's government enact structural measures to cut spending (all).

* Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi repeated his confidence that Italy will meet the three percent deficit/GDP ratio in 1997 required to join European Monetary Union. Ciampi said that Italy would also meet the other requirements, except for debt reduction, and such progress will be made sustainable by adopting permanent measures to replace some one-off provisions (all).

* Luigi Fausti, managing director of Banca Commerciale Italiana (BCI) said the bank had over three trillion lire to invest in shareholdings and was closely watching out for market opportunities. Fausti added the group expected state-controlled defence group Finmeccanica to be privatised by the end of the year. State holding IRI, which holds 60 percent of Finmeccanica, announced last week a restructuring to create a single operating unit to run the firm's industrial concerns (all).
* Retailing group Rinascente is to ask shareholders to empower it to increase capital by up to 600 billion lire (Il Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
